brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Morning edition. It covers the 24 hours to 05:10 CET on 28 October; new research covers 17:10 CET on 27 October to 05:10 CET on 28 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Russian Submarine Test-Fires a Bulava Intercontinental Missile From the Sea of Okhotsk
items.lede: The Defence Ministry says the warheads hit their target range in the Arkhangelsk region on time during what it called routine combat training.

sections.text: Russia's Defence Ministry said early on 28 October that the Pacific Fleet nuclear submarine Generalissimus Suvorov, a Borei-A class boat, fired a Bulava intercontinental ballistic missile from a submerged position in the Sea of Okhotsk [1][2]. It said the warheads reached the Chizha range in Russia's Arkhangelsk region on time, and called the launch part of planned combat training [1][2]. No launch time was given, and no Western or Ukrainian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the ministry announced the launch, but its account of the result rests on Russian state media alone, with no independent confirmation.

items.title: Russia's Defence Ministry Claims 293 Ukrainian Drones Downed in a Day
items.lede: Moscow's airports worked under flight limits, and Bryansk's governor reported more than 200 flats damaged, while Kyiv made no matching claim by the cutoff.

sections.text: Russia's Defence Ministry said on the evening of 27 October that air defences downed 71 Ukrainian drones, and 293 over the full day [3]. Russia's aviation agency said Vnukovo, Domodedovo, and Zhukovsky airports near Moscow were handling flights only with clearance because of temporary airspace restrictions [4]. Regional governors reported men injured by drones in Kursk region's Lgov and in Bryansk region, and Bryansk's governor said more than 200 flats in the city were damaged in the 27 October attack, according to Sever-Press [5]. Sever-Press also reported that two men were killed by explosive devices in Bryansk's Bezhitsky district [5]. No Ukrainian claim of targets hit was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is low on the drone totals, because they rest on the Russian Defence Ministry alone. Confidence is moderate on the airport limits and local damage, which come from Russian officials relayed by Russian outlets.

items.title: Russian Drone Hits an Apartment Block in Ukraine's Kharkiv, Injuring a Boy of Four
items.lede: Three of the four people hurt were hospitalised, and the late-evening strike set an industrial building and two homes on fire.

sections.text: A Russian drone struck Kharkiv's Osnovianskyi district in Ukraine at about 22:40 Kyiv time on 27 October (21:40 CET), hitting an apartment building where Mayor Ihor Terekhov said people were trapped [6][7]. Regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said a woman aged 32, a woman aged 65, a man aged 56, and a four-year-old boy were injured, and three were taken to hospital [8][6]. He said the strike set fire to a two-storey industrial building, a two-storey apartment building, and a one-storey house, and damaged another home and a car [8][9]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the strike and the injury count, because several outlets carry the same on-record figures from the mayor and the regional governor.

items.title: Zelensky Says Russia Has Fired Over 100 Ballistic Missiles at Kyiv Since 14 October
items.lede: Kyiv's leader tied the two-week barrage to a shortage of Patriot interceptors and said slow deliveries also weaken his hand in diplomacy.

sections.text: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said in his evening video address on 27 October that Russia has launched more than 100 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and the Kyiv region since 14 October [10]. He said Ukraine currently lacks missiles for its Patriot systems and that partners' delivery delays make it hard to defend against ballistic strikes [10]. He said stronger air-defence support would leave Ukraine in a much better position, including diplomatically, and that Russian attacks continue on Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa, Kharkiv, Sumy, and Kherson [10]. No independent count of the missiles was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that Zelensky made the statement, because it is quoted from his own address. The missile total rests on his word alone.

items.title: Ukraine-Russia Truce Widens Beyond Occupied Oleshky Across Kherson Region, Melania Trump Says
items.lede: Evacuations of the estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people left in the town are planned for Friday, and Kyiv and Moscow both say the pause is holding.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff said Ukraine began observing a ceasefire around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in the Kherson region, from 03:00 Kyiv time on 27 October (02:00 CET), and the Kremlin said Russia halted fighting there an hour later Moscow time [11][12]. On Tuesday evening U.S. First Lady Melania Trump, who brokered the pause, said on X that its area had been widened beyond Oleshky within the Kherson region to give aid convoys safe passage, citing Russia's chief of the General Staff, Valery Gerasimov [13][14]. The BBC said a Kherson city official confirmed Russian shelling had stopped in the city and the wider region, that evacuations are planned for Friday, and that an estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people remain in Oleshky [15]. Ukraine's human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said both sides were fully observing the ceasefire as of 17:30 Kyiv time, and lawmaker David Arakhamia said it runs until 22:59 Kyiv time on 1 November [16][17]. Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev called the wider zone positive news [18]. No figure for aid delivered was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the pause is holding and was widened, because Ukrainian, Russian, and U.S. figures say so on record and the BBC reports local confirmation. The Friday evacuation plan rests on the BBC's account.

items.title: Ukraine's General Staff Claims Hits on Russian Ammunition Depots in Occupied East
items.lede: The claim lists logistics sites and troop concentrations across three occupied regions, but no damage figures or imagery were released.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck Russian ammunition depots near Dyakove in the Luhansk region and near Ohorodne in the Donetsk region, and a concentration of equipment near Krasnohorivka [19]. It said logistics depots near Luhansk, Antratsyt, and Tymonove, and troop concentrations near Lahidne, Antratsyt, and Novopetrivka in Zaporizhzhia region, were also hit [19]. No damage assessment, imagery, or Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is low on the results, because they rest on a Ukrainian military claim relayed by a Ukrainian state outlet, with no independent confirmation.

items.title: Russian Drone Strikes a Fire Truck During Firefighting in Ukraine's Kramatorsk
items.lede: No firefighters were hurt, but crews in Kramatorsk and nearby Sloviansk had to suspend work at every site because of the security situation.

sections.text: Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russian strikes set a nine-storey building and private homes on fire in Kramatorsk, in the Donetsk region, and a Russian drone then hit a fire truck while crews fought the blaze [20]. No rescuers were injured [20]. In nearby Sloviansk, homes, warehouses, and a truck burned after Russian strikes [20]. The service said crews contained the fires but had to suspend work at all sites because of the security situation [20]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the account comes from Ukraine's emergency service relayed by one Ukrainian outlet, without independent confirmation.

items.title: Kharkiv Region Counts Three Dead as a Missile Injures Five in Ukraine's Derhachi
items.lede: The regional governor's Tuesday tally named two men killed in the city over the past day, and five more people were hurt in the afternoon.

sections.text: A Russian missile attack on the Novobavarskyi district of Kharkiv, Ukraine's second city, on the evening of 26 October damaged apartment buildings, private homes, and cars, and started a major fire, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said on Telegram [21]. Regional head Oleh Syniehubov said the injured included two men aged 61 and 77, a 60-year-old woman, and a 17-year-old girl [21]. Ukrinform's headline and summary said the strike killed two people, but neither the mayor nor the regional head gave a death toll [21]. Later that evening a jet-powered Russian drone attacked Chernivtsi region in western Ukraine, and its debris damaged a power facility and forced an outage, with no casualties, regional head Ruslan Osypenko said [22]. On Tuesday morning Syniehubov said two men aged 41 and 60 were killed in Kharkiv over the past day, a 60-year-old woman and a 77-year-old man were injured, and the 61-year-old man and the girl suffered acute stress reactions [23]. On Tuesday afternoon a Russian missile hit a warehouse in Derhachi, north of Kharkiv, injuring five people, he said [24]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the damage and casualty details come from Ukrainian officials relayed by one Ukrainian outlet, without independent confirmation.

items.title: Kremlin Sets No Date Yet for Abu Dhabi Talks With Ukraine and the US
items.lede: Putin told Finland's and Norway's leaders a meeting in early to mid November is agreed, while repeating that peace must meet Moscow's terms in full.

sections.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on 27 October that no date had been set for new trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the United States in Abu Dhabi [25][12]. A Kremlin readout of Putin's call that day with Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said all three welcomed an agreement to resume the talks in early to mid November [26]. The readout said Putin insisted peace requires Russia's interests to be met in full and without conditions, and blamed EU and NATO policies for prolonging the war [26]. It said the leaders also discussed Baltic Sea security [26]. A Finnish presidential readout said Stubb and Støre initiated the call in Helsinki, in consultation with Ukraine, as a follow-up to their 20 October meeting in Oslo and in connection with the upcoming meetings in Abu Dhabi, and that they spoke as leaders of their own countries, not on behalf of Europe; it did not mention a date for the talks or Putin's terms [27].

Confidence is high that the Kremlin made these statements, because they appear in its readout and Peskov's remarks. The November timing and Putin's terms rest on the Kremlin's readout alone; Finland's readout confirms the call and its link to the Abu Dhabi talks.

items.title: Russia Fires 16 Ballistic Missiles at Kyiv, Hitting a Campus and the Southern Bridge
items.lede: One woman died and 15 people were hurt, and Zelensky blamed delayed Patriot and NASAMS interceptor deliveries for letting Russian strikes through.

sections.text: Russia struck Kyiv, Ukraine's capital, with ballistic missiles in two waves, first at about 21:45 Kyiv time on 26 October (20:45 CET) and again at about 03:30 on 27 October (02:30 CET) [28][29]. The State Emergency Service said the campus of the State University of Trade and Economics, dormitories, and homes were hit, and the second wave hit an administrative building in Podilskyi district [28][30]. By Tuesday morning the toll stood at one dead, a 46-year-old woman, and 15 injured, including a paramedic and a medical technician [30][31]. Klitschko said the Southern Bridge was closed while specialists assessed damage, and metro service between Osokorky and Chervony Khutir was suspended [31]. Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched Iskander-M or S-400 missiles from Bryansk region and 280 drones from 18:00 Kyiv time on Monday, with two missiles and 255 drones downed, 25 impact sites, and debris at 16 [32][33][30]. President Volodymyr Zelensky said 16 ballistic missiles were fired overnight, called the bridge strike a serious escalation against logistics, and said delays in Patriot and NASAMS interceptor deliveries help Russia [34].
Confidence is high on the strikes, the toll, and the Air Force figures, because several outlets carry the same official numbers. The count of 16 missiles rests on Zelensky alone.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Hackers Hit Italy's Chamber of Deputies Mail System, Including Meloni's Deputy Inbox
items.lede: La Repubblica says hackers read the emails of Meloni and two other right-wing lawmakers, while Rome prosecutors wait on a police report before opening a case.

sections.text: Italy's Chamber of Deputies said its computer systems came under a large-scale cyberattack in recent days that involved the mailboxes of numerous lawmakers, including Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's account as a deputy, ANSA reported on Tuesday [1]. Palazzo Chigi sources said that mailbox is not the one Meloni uses for government communications [1] [2]. Chamber sources called the matter not an emergency and a daily occurrence, said protective measures were in place with the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) under a specific protocol, and said some system functions could be switched off temporarily [1]. The same sources said similar attempts had intensified in recent days against other national, European, and international institutions [1] [2]. Rome prosecutors are awaiting a first report from the Postal Police and will open a case for unauthorized access to a computer system [3]. La Repubblica reported on Tuesday evening that the emails of Meloni, of Delmastro, and of League lawmaker Formentini were read, and that the method, the depth of access, and the choice of targets point to a targeted operation [4]. No attribution to any actor had been made public by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the attack and Meloni's mailbox, which ANSA and Chamber sources confirm. That the emails were read rests on la Repubblica's summary alone.

items.title: Romania Blames a Russian Sabotage Ring for a Fire Beside a Brașov Arms Plant
items.lede: Bucharest summoned Moscow's ambassador and its president called the plot a grave violation of sovereignty, while the Russian Embassy rejected the accusations as unsubstantiated.

sections.text: Romania's Intelligence Service (SRI) said on 26 October that a sabotage network coordinated from Russia set the 14 September fire on the Carfil industrial platform in Brașov, next to a subsidiary of state arms maker Romarm [5][6]. Prosecutors named three suspects, two Belarusians and a Ukrainian; two are held in Germany and the third was located in Poland [6][7]. On Tuesday Foreign Minister Dan Neculăescu summoned Russia's ambassador, Vladimir Lipaev, to protest what the ministry called a clear act of hybrid warfare, and also condemned Russian attacks on merchant ships in the Black Sea [8]. President Nicușor Dan called the plot a grave violation of Romania's sovereignty and security, and Prime Minister Luca Niculescu called such attacks unacceptable [9]. The Russian Embassy said Lipaev firmly rejected the unsubstantiated accusations and that Moscow had never planned or carried out sabotage abroad, and it blamed Ukraine for threats to Black Sea shipping [10].

Confidence is high that Romania summoned the ambassador and that Russia denied the charge, because both sides' statements are on record. The Russian direction of the network rests on Romanian intelligence and prosecutors and is not independently confirmed.

items.title: Basque Police Arrest 17 After Student Riot in Bilbao
items.lede: Ten of those held are minors, all who saw a judge were freed on charges, and the groups behind the march have disowned the violence.

sections.text: Spain's Basque regional police, the Ertzaintza, have arrested 17 people over Monday night's riots in Bilbao, which followed a student demonstration against an event by the activist Vito Quiles that was finally not held, El País reported on Tuesday [1]. Ten of those detained are minors, one aged 14, and the rest are aged 18 to 25; a 22-year-old is also under investigation [1]. All who have appeared before a judge were released on charges, and none had a criminal record [1]. The police are working to identify more participants, while the groups that called the march have distanced themselves from the violence [1]. Basque government spokesperson María Ubarretxena said violence has no place in the Basque Country [1].
Confidence is high on the arrest figures, which El País attributes to the Ertzaintza; this rests on one outlet so far.

items.title: French Senate Passes Bill Making Rioters Pay for Protest Damage
items.lede: Senators voted 229 to 105 to let the state claim up to 10,000 euros from each member of a violent crowd, toughening the original text.

sections.text: France's Senate adopted the casseurs-payeurs bill early on Wednesday by 229 votes to 105, Public Sénat reported [2]. It makes everyone in a violent gathering jointly liable for damage, with the state able to claim up to 10,000 euros each, and allows seizure of welfare benefits from those who cannot pay [2]. CCI France said on Tuesday that 2,488 shops were hit on 17 October and 50 on 24 October [3]. Commerce Minister Serge Papin said resale sites had removed more than 1,700 suspect listings [4]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Saturday evening that the marches had gone smoothly despite a great many incidents of violence; on Sunday the ministry put arrests at 1,314, with 53 officers injured [5][6]. In Reims, the police watchdog IGPN was tasked with investigating after a police grenade seriously injured a marcher's shin on Saturday, franceinfo reported on Monday [7]. The Yellow Vests have called further protests for 31 Oct [6]. On Tuesday the Snes-FSU teachers' union said the government's Parcoursup concessions fall short and kept its call to march on 5 November [8].
Confidence is high on the Senate vote, the damage tallies, and the earlier arrest figures, reported on record by Public Sénat and franceinfo; the shop totals are CCI France's own.

items.title: Portugal's Ombudsman Demands Police Records on Baton Charges at Lisbon and Porto Housing Camps
items.lede: Prime Minister Luís Montenegro has now praised the officers' conduct as thousands of housing protesters massed outside parliament on Tuesday night.

sections.text: Portugal's Ombudsman, Luísa Neto, said on Monday she had urgently asked the PSP police's national directorate for documents on operations that began at about 02:00 on Sunday 25 October against housing-rights protesters camped in Lisbon's Praça D. Pedro IV and Porto's Praça D. João I, Lusa reported via RTP [9]. The interior ministry's inspectorate, IGAI, told Lusa it had opened an administrative inquiry into both operations, which left people injured [9]. The PSP dispersed the camps with batons and dogs after two hours of orders to leave, and reported 33 injured and 33 detained for disobedience; the organisers spoke of dozens injured [9]. On Tuesday evening Prime Minister Luís Montenegro praised the PSP's "careful" and "competent" work, RTP reported [10]. On Tuesday President António José Seguro called for dialogue on housing "and never violence" and said he awaited the inquiries into police conduct, Lusa reported via RTP [11]. Thousands rallied outside the Assembly of the Republic on Tuesday as the 2027 budget debate opened, and organisers said they would return to protest but not camp there [12].
Confidence is high on the ombudsman's request, the IGAI inquiry, the PSP figures, and the leaders' remarks, reported on record by Lusa and RTP; Tuesday's details rest on RTP summaries.

items.title: Thousands Rally in Prague Against Czech Plan to Scrap Public-Media Licence Fees
items.lede: Czech university students are now joining broadcaster staff in strike plans, while government politicians insist media independence is not under threat.

sections.text: Thousands filled Prague's Old Town Square in the Czech Republic on Sunday to protest a coalition bill replacing Czech Television and Czech Radio licence fees with state funding, ČTK reported [13][14]. The lower house passed the bill in first reading on Saturday; it would cut their funding by about CZK 1.4 billion [13][14]. On Monday Babiš said the coalition would not withdraw the bill and he would propose voluntary licence-fee payments [15]. On Tuesday Prague's DAMU drama faculty declared an open-ended strike alert and will join the 3 November broadcaster strike, and students in Brno and Ostrava took a similar step [16]. On Tuesday evening the unions of the National Theatre's drama company declared a strike alert, demanding the withdrawal of the funding bill and the resignation of Culture Minister Oto Klempíř, who replied that the government supports culture [17]. Chamber speaker Tomio Okamura said he would back abolishing Czech Television and Czech Radio if someone proposed it, ČT24 reported [18]. On Monday afternoon Babiš also rejected Czech Radio director René Zavoral's call for a public debate, calling him an 'activist director' who should resign [15].
Confidence is high on the protest and the vote, because ČTK and Expats.cz report them; the funding cut and the strike plan rest on Expats.cz, and no crowd estimate was published.

items.title: Italy's Salvini Vows to Press Cabinet to Halt Money and Weapons for Ukraine
items.lede: Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said Rome's line on Kyiv does not change, and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said a new Italian aid package is ready.

sections.text: Italy's deputy prime minister Matteo Salvini was confirmed as secretary of the League on Sunday with 465 votes, 76% of the 611 valid ballots, against 146 for challenger Massimo Garavaglia, at the party's congress in Milan, La Stampa and ANSA reported [19][20][21]. Three ballots were blank and five invalid, and Salvini will lead the party until 2030 [20][19]. Before the vote, Salvini said that if confirmed he would tell the Council of Ministers to stop money and arms for Ukraine [22]. On Monday Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said a new military aid package for Kyiv was ready, ANSA reported [23]. Late on Monday ANSA reported that coalition allies had halted Salvini on Kyiv, with Defence Minister Guido Crosetto saying the line does not change and Meloni irritated by his congress remarks [24]. On Tuesday, in extracts from Bruno Vespa's book due out on 2 November, Salvini said challenger Massimo Garavaglia would join the League's secretariat if he agreed, ANSA reported [25].
Confidence is high on the vote and Salvini's statements, because La Stampa and ANSA report them on record; Crosetto's reply rests on an ANSA headline and summary.

items.title: Downing Street Rows Back on Burnham's Hint of an EU Free-Movement Referendum
items.lede: Britain's business secretary now says officials from London and Brussels will discuss options, including free movement, before a 20 November summit.

sections.text: Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham, asked by broadcasters on Monday whether he could bring in EU freedom of movement without a referendum, said "no", but Downing Street later appeared to backtrack, the BBC reported [26]. Sources told the BBC no decision on a vote had been made, and his deputy spokeswoman said the government would not "get ahead" of how to consult the public [26]. She said the prime minister was not proposing a return to free movement or any option, was "not leaning either way", and thinks the Brexit deal is "not good enough" [26]. Burnham says any change would need a mandate at a general election due by 2029 [26]. On Tuesday Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds told the BBC that British and EU officials would discuss options for the relationship, including free movement, before the EU summit on 20 November, while Downing Street said its focus there is food and youth mobility deals [27]. No EU reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the statements, because the BBC quotes the prime minister, his spokeswoman, and Reynolds on record; this rests on one outlet so far.

items.title: Belgium Readies Draft Law to Nationalise Engie's Nuclear Plants if Talks Fail
items.lede: Talks with the French group are reportedly making little progress ahead of a self-imposed 4 November deadline, and ministers declined to confirm the expropriation plan.

sections.text: Belgium's federal government is preparing a fallback plan to nationalise the country's nuclear power stations, with draft legislation reportedly ready to expropriate the French energy group Engie in Belgium and compensate it, De Tijd and L'Echo reported, VRT said on Tuesday [28]. The government and Engie have negotiated since April over a state takeover of all Belgian reactors and the multi-billion bill for decommissioning them, and VRT said progress was slow [28]. The offices of Energy Minister Mathieu Bihet and Prime Minister Bart De Wever declined to confirm the plan to VRT [28]. No Engie statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate on the draft law, because VRT relays newspaper reports the government declined to confirm; the De Tijd and L'Echo originals were not read.

items.title: European Commission Proposes Making Frontex the EU's Central Agency for Migrant Returns
items.lede: The plan adds a rapid crisis force and a return-coordination centre, and the Commission says illegal crossings have more than halved in two years.

sections.text: The European Commission on Tuesday proposed strengthening the EU border agency Frontex, including a larger Standing Corps with a new European Border and Return Reserve, a Quick Reaction Force for crises, and an Online Monitoring Centre to detect threats to the borders [29]. Frontex would gain a Return Coordination Centre and could help carry out returns from third countries, and the Commission also proposed a regulation to digitalise return, readmission, and reintegration [29]. President Ursula von der Leyen said "Europe decides who comes to our Union and under what circumstances" [29]. The Commission said illegal border crossings have more than halved over two years and the return rate now exceeds 30 percent [29].
Confidence is high on the proposal's content, from the Commission's own release; the migration figures are the Commission's.

items.title: Storm Boelo Kills Two Men in Britain and Leaves Thousands Without Power
items.lede: Almost 8,000 British customers were still cut off on Tuesday as a fresh yellow wind warning covered Scotland until late evening.

sections.text: Two men were killed by falling trees in the UK on Sunday during Storm Boelo: a man in his 20s whose car was hit in Finchley, north London, at about 13:40 CET, and a 60-year-old near Castle Douglas in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, police said, the BBC reported [30]. More than 90,000 properties were without power at 20:00 CET, the Energy Networks Association said, and 838,700 lost power during Storms Austen and Boelo [30]. Gusts peaked on Sunday morning at 85mph in Machrihanish, in Argyll and Bute, the BBC reported [30]. The Portuguese-flagged freighter UHL Freedom, which lost anchor grip north of Schiermonnikoog, sailed on under limited power from 18:35 CET, the Dutch coastguard said; NOS now reports three of its 25 crew injured, down from five [31][32]. By Tuesday the Energy Networks Association said almost 8,000 were still without power, and a Met Office yellow wind warning for Scotland and northern Northern Ireland runs until 22:00 CET, with gusts up to 70mph in exposed spots [33].

Confidence is high on the deaths, the power cuts, and the Dutch freighter, because the BBC and NOS attribute them to police, the Energy Networks Association, the Met Office, and the Dutch coastguard; each country rests on one outlet.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Estonia Suspends Police and Security Service Access to Bank Data Register
items.lede: Justice Minister Pakosta said both agencies missed a 1 October deadline to install a tracker that lets citizens see who queried their accounts.

sections.text: Estonia's Justice Ministry has suspended the Police and Border Guard Board's and the Internal Security Service's access to the Enforcement Register, a state channel for querying bank account data, ERR News reported on Tuesday [1]. The agencies failed to connect to a mandatory data tracker by the 1 October deadline; the tracker lets people see who has viewed their bank data [1]. The Tax and Customs Board and bailiffs met the deadline and keep access [1]. Justice and Digital Minister Liisa Pakosta said use of the register in criminal proceedings by the two agencies is suspended until the software is ready [1]. In 2025 the Chancellor of Justice found agencies had accessed bank secrecy data without a proper legal basis [1]. No statement from the police or the Internal Security Service was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the suspension rests on one ERR report quoting the minister and an earlier ministry announcement, which was not read.

items.title: Estonia Has Detained 388 Migrants Who Crossed From Belarus Since July
items.lede: Recent detentions have all been in Tallinn, 148 people have been returned to Latvia, and 15 are suspected of organizing the smuggling.

sections.text: Estonia's Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) has detained 388 foreign nationals since July who arrived without legal basis after crossing the Belarusian border, with detentions in recent weeks taking place only in Tallinn, ERR reported on Tuesday [2]. As of Tuesday, 258 were held at the Tallinn detention center, and 148 who entered the EU via the Belarus–Latvia border had been handed back to Latvia in group transfers [2]. Fifteen people are suspected of organizing illegal migration [2]. Indrek Aru of the PPA's Northern Prefecture said some detainees had sought treatment for cold-like symptoms and skin rashes and one remained in hospital [2]. No Latvian statement on the handovers was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the figures are the border guard's own, relayed by the public broadcaster; no second outlet was read.

items.title: Latvia Extends Ban on Charter Coach Trips to Russia and Belarus Until 2027
items.lede: Riga cites the risk of intelligence gathering and recruitment on group tours, and a draft law would also halt scheduled services from 10 January.

sections.text: Latvia's government decided on Tuesday to extend for one year its ban on occasional international bus services to Russia and Belarus through the Pāternieki, Grebņeva, and Terehova crossings, to 31 October 2027, LSM reported [3]. The government cited threats to national security from organized group travel, during which participants face a significant risk of intelligence gathering and recruitment [3]. The ban applies to all carriers regardless of registration [3]. Regular scheduled services are not yet restricted, but the Transport Ministry has drafted amendments to the Road Transport Act that would ban regular and occasional bus services to Russia and Belarus, and transit through Latvia, from 10 January 2027 [3]. No Russian or Belarusian reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the decision is reported by the public broadcaster; the cabinet order itself was not read.

items.title: Estonia's Tsahkna Says Russia Shows No Sign of Wanting Talks After Putin Call
items.lede: Briefed on the Finnish and Norwegian leaders' call to the Kremlin, the foreign minister urged tighter sanctions, while Denmark's prime minister criticized the contact.

sections.text: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on Tuesday he had been briefed on that day's call between the leaders of Norway and Finland and Russian President Vladimir Putin [4]. The Finnish president's office described the call, initiated by the two countries and held in consultation with Ukraine, as a follow-up to a 20 October meeting in Oslo, aimed at conveying messages on future negotiations ahead of Russia–Ukraine meetings in Abu Dhabi [4]. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen criticized the call [4]. Tsahkna said only more pressure would make Russia take talks seriously, that there was no sign it had changed its strategic aims, and called for tighter sanctions, action on evasion, and steady support for Ukraine [4]. No Kremlin readout was read for this item.
Confidence is moderate: Tsahkna's remarks and the Finnish statement are quoted by the public broadcaster; neither the Finnish release nor a Kremlin account was read.

items.title: Lithuania's Opposition Conservatives Table Universal Conscription From 2030
items.lede: Homeland Union leader Kasčiūnas wants the draft lottery scrapped so nearly every young man on the list serves, with drone roles possibly easing physical requirements.

sections.text: Laurynas Kasčiūnas, leader of Lithuania's opposition Homeland Union–Lithuanian Christian Democrats, registered amendments on Tuesday that would replace the annual conscription quota and lottery with mandatory initial military service for nearly everyone on the draft list from 1 January 2030 [5]. Young men would be conscripted and women could serve voluntarily; exemptions, deferments, and alternative service would remain [5]. The Defence Ministry's draft list this year held 42,556 young people, of whom 5,000 were due to be called up [5]. Kasčiūnas said new warfare needs new approaches, citing drone operators who may not need strong physical training, and said the system should be designed before its cost is set [5]. He acknowledged that the conservatives did not introduce universal conscription when they led the government in 2020–2024 [5]. No response from the ruling coalition or the Defence Ministry was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the proposal's terms come from one BNS report of the party's own announcement; the amendment text was not read.

items.title: Nausėda Says Lithuania's Thaw With China Need Not Hinge on Taiwan Office Name
items.lede: The president said Vilnius could first accept chargé-level missions, with November meetings due to show whether talks with Beijing can succeed.

sections.text: Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said on Tuesday that restoring full diplomatic representation with China should not be linked directly to renaming the Taiwanese Representative Office in Vilnius, calling normalization a pragmatic goal [6]. He told Žinių Radijas that Lithuania could at first accept representation by a deputy head of mission rather than an ambassador [6]. He said it was too early to judge whether discussions with Beijing would produce results, and that meetings in November could clarify prospects [6]. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius has said he hopes for a breakthrough by year's end, and normalizing ties is in the government's program [6]. Relations soured in 2021 after Vilnius let the office open under the name "Taiwanese" rather than the "Taipei" Beijing prefers [6]. No Chinese reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the remarks are reported by one BNS account; no Chinese source was read.

items.title: More Than 200 US Troops Begin Arriving in Lithuania as Rotations Resume
items.lede: President Nausėda said the arrivals would bring the American presence to almost a third of the planned level by mid-November, after it fell to about 100 this summer.

sections.text: More than 200 American soldiers are due to arrive in Lithuania from Tuesday as Washington resumes troop rotations there, President Gitanas Nausėda told the radio station Žinių Radijas [7]. He said about 120 US soldiers were in the country and that the new arrivals would bring the force to almost a third of the number planned by mid-November [7]. The United States has rotated troops through Lithuania every nine months since 2014, but the number fell to just over 100 this summer while Washington reviewed its posture in Europe [7]. In September it was announced that two US Army battalions, more than 1,000 troops in total, would arrive at the end of October [7]. No Pentagon or US Army Europe statement on the arrivals was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the figures are the Lithuanian president's own remarks relayed by BNS; no US statement or second outlet was read.

items.title: Iran Detains Two Missing Lithuanian Women, Vilnius Confirms
items.lede: The Foreign Ministry says Tehran notified it on Monday and it is arranging consular assistance, while the prime minister says diplomats are working to free them.

sections.text: Lithuania's Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday that two Lithuanian women reported missing last week are being held in Iran, after it received official information from Tehran on 26 October [8]. The ministry gave no details of the circumstances and said it was arranging consular assistance; it repeated its advice to avoid travel to Iran and urged citizens there to leave [8]. Vilnius County police had been searching for the women, born in 1992 and 1983, who flew to Turkey in early October for tourism and then went on to Iran; relatives have not reached them since 11 October [8]. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius said active diplomatic work was under way to secure their release [8]. No Iranian statement on the charges or grounds for detention was found by the cutoff. The ELTA news agency separately received the ministry's confirmation that Iran informed it on 26 October, and the ministry declined to give details, citing privacy [9].
Confidence is high: Lithuania's Foreign Ministry confirmation is reported by both BNS and ELTA; no Iranian source was read, and the grounds for detention are not public.

items.title: Bulgaria's Government Faces Complaints Over Promoting Yotova Before the Run-Off
items.lede: Official channels urged a vote for the Radev-backed candidate, prompting an election-code complaint and a journalists' rebuke ahead of the 1 November vote.

sections.text: With all polling-station protocols processed, Bulgaria's Central Election Commission had acting President Iliana Yotova on 34.76 percent, former caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov on 31.95 percent and Revival leader Kostadin Kostadinov third, BNT reported [1]. Because no ticket won a majority, the commission on Tuesday formally set a 1 November run-off and said 1,525,034 of 6,584,025 eligible voters took part [2] [1]. Alpha Research put turnout at a record low of 22.5 percent, against 40.5 percent in 2021, as GERB and Delyan Peevski's DPS-New Beginning fielded no candidates [3]. On Monday Prime Minister Rumen Radev said voters would choose between peace and war, casting Gyurov's pro-EU, pro-Ukraine stance as warmongering [3]. The government's Facebook page and press office carried the line "Let's vote for Iliana Iotova so Bulgaria can be in safe hands," and Gyurov said this breached the electoral code; the election commission has been notified [4]. The government said no violation occurred because the run-off campaign had not started, and on Tuesday the Association of European Journalists–Bulgaria called its attempt to lecture the media dangerous [4].
Confidence is high on the run-off pairing and the commission figures, which BTA, BIRN, and BNT agree on; the dispute over official channels rests on one BIRN report.

items.title: Albania's Protesters March on Rama's Office for a 15th Day
items.lede: Tuesday's rally passed without major clashes, after police tallied over 270 arrests, while protesters again refused the prime minister's offer of dialogue.

sections.text: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama on Sunday announced a package against "violence and urban anarchy" after weeks of clashes in Tirana, blaming opposition leader Sali Berisha, "Antifa extremists", and foreign actors [5]. It would fine participants in unauthorized gatherings €100 to €1,000, and make organizing a banned gathering a criminal offense [5]. Public broadcaster RTSH reported on Monday that in 13 days of protests police had arrested more than 270 people, prosecuted 344, and suspended nine officers for excessive force [6]. The Health Ministry said on 19 October that 310 people had been injured since the protests began, including 191 police officers, Albanian Daily News reported [7]. Rama has refused to step down and offered cash bonuses to frontline police, NPR reported from Tirana on Monday [8]. On Tuesday, the 15th day, students and other protesters marched from Dibra Street to the Education Ministry, burned cardboard, and then moved on to the Prime Minister's Office, RTSH reported [9] [10]. Police held a cordon, and unlike earlier days no significant incidents were reported; protesters again rejected Rama's call for dialogue [9].

Confidence is moderate: the law's terms are Rama's own announcement relayed by BIRN, the arrest figures are official statements, and Tuesday's march is reported by RTSH and Balkanweb; no police tally for Tuesday was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Serbia's Organized-Crime Prosecutors Open Cases Against Foreign Minister Đurić and Ambassadors
items.lede: The 15 complaints concern suspected abuse of office and obstruction of diaspora voting in Sunday's election, and police have been asked to run checks.

sections.text: Serbia's Public Prosecutor's Office for Organized Crime said on Tuesday it had received 15 criminal complaints over suspected offences against electoral rights, including complaints against Foreign Minister Marko Đurić and several ambassadors, Euronews Srbija reported [11]. It first opened cases over complaints against the ambassadors to Slovakia, Aleksandar Nakić, and to the United States, Dragan Šutanovac, and on 20 October requested information from the Foreign Ministry and the Republic Electoral Commission [11]. Later complaints named the ambassadors to France, Romania, Switzerland, Bulgaria, Montenegro, Australia, Canada, and the United Arab Emirates, alleging abuse of office, violation of voting rights, and preventing voting from taking place [11]. Đurić and the ministry's security chief Vesko Radović face complaints of abuse of office and violation of voting rights, and acting Secretary-General Dušan Kozarev one of abuse of office [11]. The prosecutor asked the police organized-crime service to make checks; the statement did not say what specific acts the complaints describe [11]. No response from Đurić was found by the cutoff. Serbian public broadcaster RTS carried the same prosecutor's statement, including the 20 October requests to the ministry and election commission [12].
Confidence is high on the prosecutor's statement, which Euronews Srbija and RTS both report; the specific acts behind the complaints are not public.

items.title: Netherlands Offers Help to Armenian Exporters Squeezed by Russian Curbs
items.lede: Visiting Dutch Foreign Minister Berendsen also pledged money to trace people missing from the conflict with Azerbaijan, but sidestepped questions on Armenians held in Baku.

sections.text: Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said in Yerevan on Tuesday that the Netherlands wants to help Armenian businesses, including flower growers, find markets outside Russia, citing difficulties caused by Russian economic restrictions, JAMnews reported [1]. Speaking alongside Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan, he urged Armenia to use the EU's autonomous trade measures, approved on 24 September, which remove duties on about 80% of its exports to the EU for two years [1]. He said the Armenia–Azerbaijan peace process must end in a signed agreement and offered Dutch funding for work on the fate of people missing on both sides, which Mirzoyan welcomed [1]. Asked about Armenian prisoners in Baku, Berendsen did not answer directly [1]. No Azerbaijani reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the remarks come from one JAMnews account of the news conference; no Dutch or Armenian ministry readout was read.

items.title: Georgia's National Movement Ends Its Defense in Party-Ban Hearings
items.lede: A National Movement representative called Georgian Dream's suit political gossip, and Coalition for Change presents its case on Wednesday, with hearings scheduled to run to 30 October.

sections.text: Georgia's Constitutional Court began substantive hearings on Monday on a lawsuit by 88 Georgian Dream MPs to declare five opposition parties unconstitutional: Unity – National Movement, Coalition for Change, Lelo – Strong Georgia, Gakharia for Georgia, and the Federalists [2]. The suit accuses them of seeking to overthrow the constitutional order and of denying the authorities' legitimacy, and blames the National Movement for the 2008 war with Russia; all five reject the allegations [2]. The court partly granted a final defense motion on evidence but refused to call Bidzina Ivanishvili, Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, Tbilisi Mayor Kakha Kaladze, and other ruling-party figures as witnesses, after rejecting 13 earlier witness motions [2]; The Messenger confirmed the partial evidence ruling and the refusal to summon Ivanishvili [3]. Court President Revaz Nadaraya repeatedly rebuked National Movement representative Zaza Bibilashvili, who argued that upholding the suit would legitimize Russia's 2008 aggression [2]. On Tuesday, day five, three National Movement representatives closed its defense; Ana Tsitlidze called the suit "political gossip, myths and manipulation" and questioned the judges' impartiality [4]. Coalition for Change is due to present on 28 October, and hearings run to 30 October [4].
Confidence is high on the court's earlier rulings, which JAMnews and The Messenger both report; Tuesday's courtroom exchanges rest on JAMnews alone.

items.title: Putin Calls Azerbaijan a Reliable Partner at Moscow Gas Exporters' Summit
items.lede: The Russian leader cited an active energy dialogue with Aliyev and said Russia supplies Turkey with up to 30 billion cubic meters of gas.

sections.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Tuesday that Azerbaijan is a stable and reliable partner for Moscow in many areas, speaking at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit in Moscow, News.am reported [5]. He stressed an active dialogue with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev on expanding energy cooperation and said Russia supplies Turkey with up to 30 billion cubic meters of natural gas [5]. No Kremlin transcript or Azerbaijani response was read by the cutoff.
Confidence is low: the remarks come from one Armenian outlet's summary; the Kremlin transcript was not read.

items.title: EU Commits €38 Million to Georgian Citizens While Withholding Government Aid
items.lede: Brussels keeps more than €120 million in direct assistance frozen over democratic backsliding, steering new money to towns, farms, and civil society.

sections.text: The European Union will allocate €38 million ($42 million) to new projects for people across Georgia while continuing to withhold direct financial support from the Georgian government over democratic backsliding, OC Media reported on Tuesday [6]. The projects cover economic opportunities in towns, labor-market skills, rural women and family farms, violence against women and girls, safe migration, and civil society [6]. The EU in Georgia said it no longer funds the authorities but continues to deliver assistance to the people [6]. The Commission suspended more than €120 million in bilateral aid to the authorities in June 2024, after the Council concluded Georgia's accession process had effectively halted [6]. No Georgian Dream reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the allocation is reported by OC Media citing the EU delegation; the delegation's statement itself was not read.

items.title: Russian Food-Safety Inspectors to Audit Georgia's Fruit Exports From 2 November
items.lede: The Rosselkhoznadzor visit, the first of its kind since 2014, follows Moscow's suspension of some Georgian drinks imports this month.

sections.text: Russia's agricultural watchdog Rosselkhoznadzor announced on Monday that it will visit Georgia from 2 November to inspect the phytosanitary certification system for fruit exported to Russia, OC Media reported on Tuesday [7]. The delegation will examine certification of pome and stone fruit and audit a laboratory that tests plant products for pesticide residues; the last such inspection was in 2014 [7]. The agency said the visit was arranged at the invitation of Georgia's National Food Agency [7]. It follows Russia's temporary suspension this month of imports and sales of some Georgian alcoholic and soft drinks, which Moscow attributed to quality control and denied was political [7]. Georgia and Russia have had no diplomatic relations since the 2008 war but still trade [7]. No Georgian government comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the visit rests on the Russian agency's announcement as relayed by OC Media; the agency's release was not read.

items.title: Azerbaijan Rebuffs Iran's University Offer to Girls Hit by School Hijab Rules
items.lede: Baku's education ministry called Tehran's offer interference, and a Turkish presidential adviser who criticized the rules has quit, at Baku's request per RFE/RL, a claim JAMnews says is unconfirmed.

sections.text: Azerbaijan and Iran have traded accusations over Azerbaijan's new secular school-uniform rules, which effectively ban hijabs in schools, after Iran offered to admit Azerbaijani girls to its universities, JAMnews reported on Tuesday [8]. Azerbaijan's Ministry of Science and Education called the remarks inappropriate interference and noted that Iran has no schools teaching in Azerbaijani despite an estimated 40 million ethnic Azerbaijanis there [8]. Representatives of 55 Azerbaijani NGOs wrote to Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian seeking Azerbaijani-language education [8]. Oktay Saral, an adviser to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, stepped down after criticizing the rules; RFE/RL's Azerbaijani service said he resigned at Baku's request, a claim JAMnews said had not been confirmed [8]. No Iranian government response to the ministry was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the ministry statement and the resignation are relayed in one JAMnews digest, the latter citing RFE/RL; neither original was read.

items.title: Hesse's CDU Leader Ines Claus Emerges as a Contender for Germany's Presidency
items.lede: Merz's circle denies she is his favourite, and the move sets up a possible clash with the CSU, which backs Ilse Aigner.

sections.text: Ines Claus, 49, who leads the CDU group in Hesse's state parliament and is a deputy federal CDU chair, told the Rheinische Post on Tuesday it was a great honour to be named as a possible successor to President Frank-Walter Steinmeier [1]. The paper cited senior CDU sources calling her Chancellor Friedrich Merz's favourite, which his circle clearly denied, saying he had neither decided nor made a proposal [1]. Leading CDU politicians told dpa a bid would fail for lack of a national profile, and CSU voices called it a trial balloon [1]. The CSU has so far proposed Bavarian parliament speaker Ilse Aigner; CDU bodies are due to discuss the question on 9 November, and the Federal Convention votes on 30 January [2].

Confidence is high on Claus's statement and the Merz camp denial, reported by dpa via the Tagesspiegel and by tagesschau. Confidence is moderate on her standing in the party, which rests on unnamed sources.

items.title: IG Metall Rejects Employers' First Offer for Germany's 3.7 Million Metalworkers
items.lede: Warning strikes can begin on Sunday when the peace obligation ends, after talks also failed in Bavaria, Lower Saxony, and Baden-Württemberg.

sections.text: Germany's IG Metall union on Tuesday rejected the first offer from metal and electrical industry employers in regional talks covering just over 3.7 million workers [3] [4]. Employers in five bargaining regions jointly offered, for the first time, a one-off payment of 1 percent of annual pay in July 2027 and a permanent 1.3 percent rise in July 2028, with a contract running to the end of 2028 [3] [4]. North Rhine-Westphalia district head Knut Giesler called it a de facto minus round; the Lower Saxony district said warning strikes from 1 November were unavoidable [3]. Gesamtmetall president Udo Dinglreiter said job losses and deindustrialisation had to be stopped [3]. Südwestmetall said almost half of Baden-Württemberg firms, 45 percent, would not have to pay the one-off sum under a hardship clause [4].
Confidence is high on the offer terms, the rejection, and the strike timetable, reported by tagesschau and dpa via the FAZ from union and employer statements.

items.title: Car Rams a Group in Germany's Lower Saxony as Police Open Fire
items.lede: Three people were provisionally detained, and police, who do not suspect a terror attack, are investigating the late-Monday ramming in connection with clan crime.

sections.text: A car was deliberately driven into a group of people in Neustadt am Rübenberge, near Hannover in Germany's Lower Saxony, late on Monday evening, injuring at least five, some seriously but none critically [5] [6]. Officers at a nearby traffic check fired at the BMW to stop it; the driver fled on foot and left the car behind [6] [7]. Police provisionally arrested three people at the address of the presumed vehicle owner and are checking whether they were involved [7] [5]. Police do not treat it as a terror attack; those involved apparently knew each other, and the investigation is linked to clan crime [5] [7]. No arrest warrant or charge had been reported by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the incident, injuries, police shots, and arrests, reported by NDR, ZDFheute, and dpa via the Stuttgarter Zeitung from police statements. Confidence is moderate on the clan link, which rests on early police findings.

items.title: German Environment Minister Says Audi's U.S. Plant Bets on a Dead Horse
items.lede: Criticism of Döllner's Georgia rally appearance now reaches the federal cabinet, days before Audi reports third-quarter figures on Friday.

sections.text: German carmaker Audi, part of Volkswagen, plans a $4.2 billion, 4,500-job first U.S. plant in Georgia, which President Trump announced at a Republican rally on Saturday with Audi chief Gernot Döllner onstage [8] [9] [10]. VW works council head Daniela Cavallo and IG Metall chief Christiane Benner accused Döllner of breaching Audi's neutrality rules [11] [12]. Baden-Württemberg's premier Cem Özdemir said anyone investing in Georgia must say what happens in Neckarsulm [10], where A5 and A6 output is due to end in late 2033 [13]. In an internal letter seen by dpa, Döllner wrote on Tuesday that Audi was asked to present the plans with the president, decided solely in the company's interest, and that its U.S. business is not profitable today [14]. In a YouGov poll of 2,725 adults on 26 October, 57 percent called the appearance inappropriate and 18 percent appropriate [14]. A German government spokesperson declined to comment, calling it a business decision [12]. Federal Environment Minister Carsten Schneider (SPD) told the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger that Audi was betting on fossil fuels, a dead horse [15] [16]. Audi reports third-quarter figures on Friday [15].

Confidence is high on the quotes and the plant plan, reported by tagesschau, The Guardian, stern, and the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger. Confidence is moderate on any rule breach, which rests on labor leaders' reading.

items.title: Germany Narrows Its Nuclear Waste Repository Search to Under 5% of Its Territory
items.lede: Six states have now dropped out entirely, Baden-Württemberg's Ulm region is also out, and the Bundestag will have the final say on the site.

sections.text: Germany's federal repository company BGE said on Tuesday that areas it considers geologically suitable for a high-level nuclear waste repository now cover less than five percent of the country, and that all of Germany has now been assessed [17]. Rhineland-Palatinate, Hesse, Berlin, Saxony, Hamburg, and Saarland are no longer part of the search; Saxony, Berlin, Hamburg, and Hesse were dropped this year [17]. In 2020 the company had named 90 sub-areas covering almost 54 percent of Germany; granite, salt, and clay are considered potentially suitable host rocks [17]. In Baden-Württemberg, the Ulm region was rated well suited but not among the best areas and has dropped out, the Stuttgarter Zeitung reported [18]. The BGE plans to propose five to ten regions for surface exploration by the end of 2027; the ratings are not legally binding, and the Bundestag decides the final site [18] [17].

Confidence is high on the narrowing and the states dropped, which tagesschau reports from a BGE press release. Confidence is high on the Ulm rating, reported by the Stuttgarter Zeitung from the same BGE announcement.

items.title: German Top Court Sends Künast's Fake-Quote Case Against Meta to the EU Court
items.lede: The Luxembourg judges must now decide whether platforms must proactively find and remove copies of unlawful posts, a question with Europe-wide reach.

sections.text: Germany's Federal Court of Justice on Tuesday referred Green politician Renate Künast's lawsuit against Meta to the European Court of Justice for a preliminary ruling, staying the case (VI ZR 64/24) [19] [20]. Künast wants Facebook to delete all essentially identical variants of a meme attributing to her a quote she never said, without her having to flag each post, and seeks at least 10,000 euros in compensation [19]. Meta argues that as a neutral hosting provider it only has to remove specifically identified posts [19]. A Frankfurt appeals court upheld her injunction claim in 2024 but rejected damages [19].
Confidence is high on the referral and the parties' positions, reported by tagesschau and the legal news site LTO.

items.title: Munich Court Keeps Neo-Nazi Terrorist Zschäpe Jailed Until at Least 2035
items.lede: The decision is not yet final, and if upheld she would be at least 60 years old before any release.

sections.text: The Higher Regional Court in Munich, Germany, set a minimum term of 24 years for Beate Zschäpe, the convicted member of the neo-Nazi terror group NSU, rejecting her bid for early release in a decision dated 23 October and made public on Tuesday [21] [22]. Zschäpe was sentenced to life in 2018 as an accomplice to the NSU murders of nine people with immigrant backgrounds and a policewoman [21]. Having served about 15 years, the legal minimum, she applied for release, citing her break with far-right views and her participation in a non-state neo-Nazi exit program [21]. The court credited her admission and expressions of shame but ruled that these did not outweigh her exceptionally grave guilt [21]. The ruling is not yet final; the defense and the federal prosecutor can appeal [21].
Confidence is high on the ruling and its terms, reported by tagesschau with BR and by the legal news site LTO from the court's decision.

items.title: Germany's Long-Term Care Reform Commission Begins Work on Stable Contributions
items.lede: Thirteen experts must find ways to finance care insurance without sharp contribution rises, as an eight-billion-euro gap looms next year.

sections.text: Germany's long-term care structural commission, set up by the federal government almost two weeks ago, officially began work on Tuesday [23]. The 13-member expert panel, chaired by former Caritas secretary general Georg Cremer and Gabriele Kuhn-Zuber, is to propose a reform that keeps care insurance contributions stable into the years after 2030 [23]. The cabinet agreed in late September on a law meant to close a funding gap of about eight billion euros expected in the care insurance next year [23]. The SPD's proposed cap on care costs was blocked by the CDU, and the commission is now to examine whether and how the co-payments borne by people in care can be limited, as well as models for social equalisation between statutory and private care insurance [23]. The substitute health insurers' association vdek welcomed the start but warned that, despite the planned reform law, the care insurance faces a deficit of over one billion euros in 2027 [24].
Confidence is high on the commission's start, confirmed by tagesschau and a vdek statement. Confidence is high on membership and mandate, reported by tagesschau.
